newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar edges up, MCI tightens after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar edges up, MCI tightens after jobs data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar rose and bill rates stood still on Tuesday after Statistics New Zealand issued jobs data for the June quarter.
The kiwi dollar was quoted at US$0.6430/37 compared with US$0.6427/34 just before the data was released.
The MCI came in to about 87 basis points below the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's desired level before dipping back to about 90 basis points under, or 735 on the index.
Ninety-day bill rates edged up slightly to 8.32 percent from 8.29 percent before the release.

Markets, and most economists polled by Reuters, had been expecting the data to show more weakness in jobs growth than the outturn and to show hours worked in the quarter rising by less than an RBNZ estimate of 1.9 percent.
The actual hours worked data showed a rise of 2.5 percent in the quarter.
